title: ESG Scores & Credit Spreads
subtitle: The relationship between ESG quality and credit pricing across fixed income sectors
source_note: Illustrative dataset based on public ESG and OAS data patterns across Asia-Pacific and global credit markets. Not investment advice.
finding_1_title: ESG Quality Commands a Spread Premium
finding_1_text: The negative correlation between ESG scores and OAS across sectors is statistically observable: higher-rated issuers on ESG dimensions tend to trade tighter particularly within investment-grade credit. Sovereign and quasi-sovereign issuers anchor the upper-left quadrant.
finding_2_title: Sector Dispersion Matters More Than the Average
finding_2_text: The cross-sectional dispersion within sectors - especially Real Estate and Energy - is more revealing than aggregate trends. Within-sector ESG differentiation represents the actionable alpha opportunity for a bottom-up credit selector.
finding_3_title: High Yield Shows the Steepest ESG Gradient
finding_3_text: Sub-investment-grade issuers show the widest spread range relative to ESG score movement. This suggests ESG risk is being repriced more aggressively in the riskier part of the credit spectrum - consistent with increased institutional exclusion mandates.

title: Asia Credit Sector Allocation
subtitle: Portfolio composition and risk contribution by sector across the credit book
source_note: Illustrative portfolio breakdown. For demonstration purposes only. Actual allocations subject to mandate constraints and investment committee approval.
finding_1_text: Financial institutions represent the largest allocation reflecting their stronger governance frameworks, regulatory capital requirements, and liquidity profiles relative to corporate issuers in Asia-Pacific markets.
finding_2_text: China real estate stress events prompted a structural underweight in the sector. Remaining exposure concentrated in Hong Kong-listed developers with demonstrated offshore refinancing access and diversified asset bases.
finding_3_text: Regulated utilities provide attractive risk-adjusted carry with lower default rates historically. Growing green bond issuance in this sector aligns with ESG mandate requirements while maintaining spread contribution.

title: Credit Quality Migration
subtitle: Rating transition trends across the investment-grade and high-yield spectrum over time
source_note: Based on illustrative rating transition patterns consistent with published agency migration matrices. Illustrative only.
finding_1_text: Investment-grade issuers showed higher net upgrade activity driven by improving balance sheet metrics in Financials and Utilities. The HY-to-IG crossover pipeline grew meaningfully in the review period.
finding_2_title: Fallen Angel Risk Elevated in Real Estate
finding_2_text: Downgrade velocity in the Real Estate sector accelerated with multiple previously IG-rated names migrating to HY. This created forced selling pressure and spread widening beyond fundamental value.
finding_3_text: Issuers with improving ESG trajectories demonstrated statistically lower downgrade rates compared to sector peers - reinforcing the integration of ESG momentum as a forward-looking credit signal.

title: Spread Compression Trend
subtitle: Quarterly average OAS movement across investment-grade and high-yield credit
source_note: Illustrative quarterly spread trend consistent with broad market direction over the period shown. For demonstration purposes only.
finding_1_title: Both Segments Compressed Through the Cycle
finding_1_text: Investment-grade and high-yield spreads both tightened meaningfully over the eight-quarter window reflecting improving credit conditions and strong technical demand from yield-seeking allocators.
finding_2_text: HY spreads compressed by over 25% from peak while IG compressed by a smaller proportion - typical of a risk-on credit cycle where lower-quality paper re-rates faster than higher-quality paper.
finding_3_text: A modest widening in Q3 24 across both segments coincided with a macro risk-off episode but normalised quickly, reinforcing the view that the underlying credit fundamentals remained intact through the period.

title: Issuer Site Visit - Due Diligence
subtitle: A first-hand look at on-site due diligence as part of the credit underwriting process
source_note: Photo documentation from an issuer site visit conducted as part of the fundamental credit review process.
finding_1_text: Site visits surface operational realities that financial statements alone cannot - asset quality, management bandwidth, and execution capability are best assessed in person, particularly for asset-heavy credits.
finding_2_text: Conversations with operational management, not just the IR team, often reveal the gap between strategy and execution - informing both the credit view and the engagement priorities post-investment.
finding_3_text: On-site visits also build the long-term issuer relationship that supports better information flow during periods of stress - an underrated input to active credit risk management.

title: Sustainable Equity Allocation Note
subtitle: A scenario-based framework for climate transition risk in strategic asset allocation
source_note: Sample research note. Full document available via the link below the preview.
finding_1_text: The framework compares orderly, disorderly, and delayed climate transition pathways, translating each into a concrete equity tilt and expected tracking error rather than a single static assumption.
finding_2_title: Disorderly Transition Carries the Largest Tilt
finding_2_text: A disorderly transition scenario implies the largest required shift toward low-carbon equity exposure - underscoring the asymmetric cost of policy delay versus an orderly, well-telegraphed transition path.
finding_3_text: The output feeds directly into fund-level climate target-setting and manager mandate language, translating scenario analysis into governance-ready policy commitments rather than a standalone research exercise.
